title: Introduce workload deglitcher + tail-response smoothing and cost-tuner CLI
author: Sofia Liang
description: Context: production traces showed recurring short-duration high-concurrency spikes ('glitches') that push the serving stack into suboptimal batching and cache-miss behavior, increasing unit cost for low-traffic routes while degrading p95 latency for tail requests. Motivation: existing econ defaults are great for steady-state workloads but oscillate badly on bursty tails; operators end up widening SLAs or creating ad-hoc route overrides. This PR introduces a two-pronged, conservative change set to reduce unit-cost oscillation and make defaults safer for bursty, low-volume routes: 1) A lightweight 'workload deglitcher' signature detector integrated in the request router that detects short spikes (configurable 1-5 minute windows) and applies a transient smoothing policy: prefer smaller micro-batches, enable conservative KV prefix caching prioritization, and temporarily pin to a lower-quantization fallback when latency SLOs are relaxed. 2) A 'tail-response smoothing' module in the runtime scheduler that stretches the effective batching window only for detected glitch windows to trade a few ms of median latency for dramatically lower per-token cost at the tail. 3) A small companion CLI tool (redwood-cost-tuner) and library under tools/econ-sim that lets SREs/Platform engineers run fast Monte Carlo simulations of route-level unit economics across combinations of batch_size, kv_cache_policy, and quant_profiles; the tool includes presets and an automated 'safe-default' suggester that writes YAML snippets for per-route defaults. Changes: added workload_deglitcher.py (router integration), tail_smoother.py (scheduler hook), a new conservative quant profile (qsafe-i16) with runtime gating, the cost-tuner CLI (tools/econ-sim/cli.py) and a lightweight simulation engine (tools/econ-sim/sim.py), and docs + smoke tests. Backwards compatibility: all behavior is opt-in by default; the global config flag runtime.enable_deglitcher is false unless set by ops or via the safe-default suggester. Rollout plan: feature gate off, deploy to staging; run cost-tuner against staging traffic and generate suggested per-route configs; flip feature gate to enabled only for routes in a canary list for 72 hours and monitor p50/p95/units-per-req. Observability: new tracing spans (router.deglitch.detect, scheduler.tail_smooth.apply) and metrics (deglitch.window_count, tail_smooth_applied, econ_sim_recommendations) included. Risks & mitigations: initial perf run indicated qsafe-i16 caused a 2% token throughput regression on LLM-7B float paths; we narrowed the runtime gate for qsafe-i16 to routes with sequence_length < 1024 and added a GC-friendly quant fallback. Tests: unit tests for detection heuristics and simulation engine; integration smoke for router->scheduler wiring. Deployment notes: config schema bump (runtime.enable_deglitcher boolean, econ_suggester.bucket_ms int). Related: ENG-1423 (workload stability), ENG-1487 (unit econ tooling).

review_comments: Diego Ramirez: Overall this looks promising. Two concerns: make the detection window configurable per-route and ensure metric cardinality doesn't explode when used org-wide.

Sofia Liang: Addressed both — detection window is now per-route with global fallback and deglitcher emits aggregated metrics by route-prefix only (dropped fine-grain user ids). Added docs section on cardinality.
Maya Patel: The qsafe-i16 profile causes a 2% throughput regression on some kernels in perf runs. Can we gate it by seq_len and add a fast fallback?
Sofia Liang: Yes — updated runtime gating so qsafe-i16 is only selected for seq_len < 1024 and added a hysteresis-based quick-fallback when observed throughput drops >3%.
Alexei Volkov: Add a canary rollout playbook and a pre-merge smoke job that runs econ-sim against recorded traces. Also please add a small e2e test verifying the suggester emits valid YAML.
Sofia Liang: Added playbook and the e2e test. CI now runs econ-sim against a tiny trace blob (deterministic seed).
checks: CI/perf-bench: initial fail (qprofile regression) -> rerun pass after gating tweak
release_notes: New opt-in workload deglitcher and tail-response smoothing to reduce unit-cost oscillation for bursty routes. Includes redwood-cost-tuner CLI to simulate unit economics and generate safe-default route configs. Qsafe-i16 quant profile added (gated).
